text: The authors note that with a stochastic oracle, changes of order 1/T in the oracle's distribution can add up to an O(1) change in output probability over a time-T computation, so they require the machine M to be K-Lipschitz at oracle O. This means that for any other oracle O', the change in M's acceptance probability is less than K times the largest change in the oracle's answer probabilities.
title: K-Lipschitz assumption for debate with a stochastic human-judgement oracle
